source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which lymph nodes represent the primary echelon of drainage for the thyroid gland?
explanation: Primary drainage is to central compartment lymph nodes.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following conditions is usually present with hyperthyroidism?
explanation: Graves’ disease is the most common cause of primary hyperthyroidism.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: What are the manifestations of thyrotoxicosis?
answer_text: Irritability. | Hair loss. | Muscle weakness and wasting. | Hyperkinesias. | Heart failure.
explanation: Excess thyroid hormone causes neuropsychiatric symptoms, hair loss, muscle weakness and may lead to heart failure.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following are associated with Graves’ disease?
answer_text: Pretibial myxoedema. | Exposure keratitis. | Optic neuropathy. | Chemosis. | Lymphoid hyperplasia.
explanation: Graves’ disease involves eye signs including myxoedema, keratitis, optic neuropathy, chemosis and lymphoid changes.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following are true regarding medical therapy for thyrotoxicosis?
option_A: Propranolol and nadolol reduce free T3 (fT3) and free T4 (fT4) levels.
option_B: Antithyroid drugs most often cure thyrotoxicosis due to a toxic nodule.
option_C: Carbimazole can be safely given in pregnancy and lactation.
option_D: Agranulocytosis is an uncommon problem with antithyroid drugs.
option_E: Patients with ophthalmopathy respond best to medical management.
answer_text: Agranulocytosis is an uncommon problem with antithyroid drugs.
explanation: Only agranulocytosis is true; the beta‐blockers do not lower thyroid hormones, antithyroid drugs rarely cure toxic nodules and carbimazole is contraindicated in pregnancy.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Surgery is the preferred option of treatment in which of the following cases of thyrotoxicosis?
option_C: Pregnant mothers not adequately controlled with medications.
answer_text: A diffuse toxic goitre. | Severe manifestations of Graves’ ophthalmopathy. | Pregnant mothers not adequately controlled with medications. | Relapse of Graves’ disease. | Presence of local compressive symptoms.
explanation: Surgery is indicated for diffuse goitre, severe ophthalmopathy, inadequate control in pregnancy, relapse and compressive symptoms.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following are indications for radioiodine treatment?
explanation: Radioiodine treatment is indicated for relapsed Graves’ disease and multinodular goitre only.
topics: Graves disease; Toxic multinodular goitre; Goitre

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following are true in neonatal hypothyroidism?
option_A: Endemic cretinism is due to iodine deficiency.
option_C: Biochemical screening for hypothyroidism is carried out on all neonates in the United Kingdom.
option_D: Radioactive iodine treatment is safe after the first trimester of pregnancy.
option_E: Women on antithyroid drugs may give birth to a hypothyroid baby.
answer_text: Endemic cretinism is due to iodine deficiency. | Macroglossia is a clinical feature. | Biochemical screening for hypothyroidism is carried out on all neonates in the United Kingdom. | Women on antithyroid drugs may give birth to a hypothyroid baby.
explanation: Screening is routine; iodine deficiency, macroglossia and maternal antithyroid drugs are implicated, while radioactive iodine is contraindicated.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Myxoedema can present as the following:
answer_text: Complete heart block. | Ventricular tachycardia. | Mania. | Shortness of breath. | Sepsis.
explanation: Severe hypothyroidism (myxoedema) may cause conduction abnormalities, arrhythmias, neuropsychiatric issues, dyspnea and sepsis.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Biochemically, hypothyroidism can be associated with the following:
answer_text: Hyponatraemia. | Hyperlipidaemia. | Thyroid peroxidase (TPO) autoantibodies. | Raised TSH. | Low fT3 and fT4.
explanation: All of these biochemical features are seen in hypothyroidism.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Hypothyroidism could be a presenting feature in which of the following conditions?
answer_text: Sarcoidosis. | Pituitary lesions. | Thyroiditis. | Iodine deficiency.
explanation: It presents in sarcoidosis, pituitary lesions, thyroiditis and iodine deficiency; benzodiazepine treatment is not a cause.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following statements regarding thyroid neoplasms are true?
option_A: Papillary carcinoma is the most common.
option_B: Men and women are equally affected.
option_C: Thyroid cancer is most common after the age of 70 years.
option_D: Medullary carcinoma originates from the C-cells.
option_E: Anaplastic carcinoma is the least common.
answer_text: Papillary carcinoma is the most common. | Medullary carcinoma originates from the C-cells. | Anaplastic carcinoma is the least common.
explanation: Papillary carcinoma is most common, medullary carcinoma arises from C-cells and anaplastic carcinoma is rare.
topics: Papillary thyroid carcinoma; Medullary thyroid carcinoma; Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following statements regarding thyroglobulin are true?
option_A: It is part of normal thyroid function tests.
option_B: It is secreted only by cancerous cells.
option_C: Autoantibodies may interfere with its levels.
option_D: It is a sensitive marker of recurrence of differentiated thyroid cancer.
answer_text: Autoantibodies may interfere with its levels. | It is a sensitive marker of recurrence of differentiated thyroid cancer. | Radioiodine treatment affects its concentration.
explanation: Autoantibodies can interfere with its measurement, and thyroglobulin is used as a marker for recurrence and is affected by radioiodine therapy.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Regarding papillary and follicular cancer, which of the following statements are true?
option_A: Lymph node metastasis is more common in follicular cancer than in papillary cancer.
option_B: In papillary cancer, central lymph node metastases are associated with decreased survival.
option_C: Distant metastasis is more common in the follicular variety.
option_D: Hurthle cell carcinoma is a type of follicular cancer.
answer_text: Distant metastasis is more common in the follicular variety. | Hurthle cell carcinoma is a type of follicular cancer. | Papillary carcinoma is usually slow-growing.
explanation: Follicular cancer more often has distant metastases, Hurthle cell carcinoma is a variant and papillary carcinoma is generally indolent.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following statements are true when a preoperative diagnosis of a differentiated thyroid cancer is made?
option_A: Whole-body MRI or CT imaging is essential.
option_B: Lobectomy is recommended for tumours less than 1 cm.
option_C: Elective lateral nodal dissection should be performed.
option_D: Routine central compartment node clearance is not essential for small tumours.
option_E: The absence of a rising thyroglobulin excludes recurrence.
answer_text: Lobectomy is recommended for tumours less than 1 cm. | Routine central compartment node clearance is not essential for small tumours.
explanation: For small differentiated thyroid cancers, a lobectomy with limited central node clearance is recommended.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following statements regarding medullary thyroid cancers are true?
option_A: It can present as multiple endocrine neoplasia.
option_C: It is associated with a poor prognosis.
option_E: High levels of calcitonin and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) are typical.
answer_text: It can present as multiple endocrine neoplasia. | It is not TSH-dependent. | Diarrhoea is a common feature. | High levels of calcitonin and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) are typical.
explanation: Medullary carcinoma is part of MEN syndromes, is TSH-independent, may cause diarrhoea and is characterized by high calcitonin/CEA.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Regarding primary hyperparathyroidism, which of the following statements are true?
option_B: Hypercalcaemia triggers the release of parathyroid hormone (PTH).
option_C: Familial hyperparathyroidism commonly presents as an adenoma.
option_E: Hyperparathyroidism can be associated with a pituitary adenoma.
answer_text: Primary hyperparathyroidism is usually sporadic. | Hyperparathyroidism can be associated with a pituitary adenoma.
explanation: It is usually sporadic and may be associated with pituitary adenomas; normally hypercalcaemia suppresses PTH.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following suggest a biochemical diagnosis of primary hyperparathyroidism?
option_A: Raised ionised calcium and suppressed PTH levels.
option_B: Raised total calcium and elevated PTH levels.
option_E: Raised ionised calcium and elevated PTH levels.
answer_text: Raised total calcium and elevated PTH levels. | Low serum phosphate levels. | Raised ionised calcium and elevated PTH levels.
explanation: High total and ionised calcium with elevated PTH and low phosphate indicate primary hyperparathyroidism.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following are associated with hypercalcaemia?
answer_text: Thyrotoxicosis. | Chronic renal failure (CRF). | Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia (FHH). | Sarcoidosis. | Milk alkali syndrome.
explanation: All are causes of hypercalcaemia; in chronic renal failure it arises with tertiary hyperparathyroidism or calcium/vitamin D therapy.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following are operative indications for primary hyperparathyroidism?
answer_text: Renal stones. | Low bone density. | Renal impairment. | Young age.
explanation: Operative treatment is indicated for renal stones, low bone density, renal impairment and young age; a mildly elevated calcium is not sufficient.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Regarding operation for primary hyperparathyroidism, which of the following statements are correct?
option_C: Recurrent laryngeal nerve damage can occur in about 5%–7% of cases.
option_D: Endoscopic technique is the most favoured operative mode.
option_E: Gamma probes can be used for exploratory purposes.
answer_text: Permanent hypoparathyroidism is likely. | PTH can be measured intraoperatively. | Gamma probes can be used for exploratory purposes.
explanation: There is a risk of permanent hypoparathyroidism, intraoperative PTH measurement is used and gamma probes may assist; nerve injury rates and endoscopic use are lower.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following statements are true regarding imaging of the parathyroid gland?
option_A: High-frequency ultrasound can identify nearly 75% of enlarged glands.
option_B: Technetium-99m-labelled sestamibi scan identifies around 90% of enlarged glands.
option_C: Single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) scan can influence surgical approach.
option_D: CT and MRI must be undertaken prior to first-time neck exploration.
option_E: Adenomas weighing less than 500 mg show reduced concordance with imaging.
answer_text: High-frequency ultrasound can identify nearly 75% of enlarged glands. | Single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) scan can influence surgical approach. | Adenomas weighing less than 500 mg show reduced concordance with imaging.
explanation: Ultrasound has ~75% sensitivity, SPECT can guide surgery and small adenomas are harder to detect.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following statements are true regarding operative strategies for the parathyroid?
option_A: In a conventional approach, a transverse collar incision is made.
option_B: In a targeted approach, a 2–3-cm incision is made over the site of the adenoma.
option_C: In patients with four-gland disease, transcervical thymectomy is not recommended.
option_D: In multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN-1), total parathyroidectomy reduces the risk of recurrence.
option_E: Preoperative imaging can identify nearly 10% of patients with mediastinal adenoma.
answer_text: In a conventional approach, a transverse collar incision is made. | In a targeted approach, a 2–3-cm incision is made over the site of the adenoma. | In multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN-1), total parathyroidectomy reduces the risk of recurrence.
explanation: Conventional and targeted incisions are correct and in MEN-1 total parathyroidectomy is advised; the other statements are false.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following statements are correct regarding hypoparathyroidism?
option_A: Serum calcium must be checked within 24 hours of total thyroidectomy.
option_B: Serum calcium levels below 1.9 mmol/L can pose a medical emergency.
option_C: Chvostek’s sign is suggestive of hypercalcaemia.
option_D: DiGeorge syndrome is a medical cause of hypoparathyroidism.
option_E: Cardiac arrhythmias can occur during an episode of hypocalcaemia.
answer_text: Serum calcium must be checked within 24 hours of total thyroidectomy. | Serum calcium levels below 1.9 mmol/L can pose a medical emergency. | DiGeorge syndrome is a medical cause of hypoparathyroidism. | Cardiac arrhythmias can occur during an episode of hypocalcaemia.
explanation: Calcium must be monitored post-thyroidectomy, levels below 1.9 mmol/L are dangerous, DiGeorge syndrome causes hypoparathyroidism and hypocalcaemia may lead to arrhythmias.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following statements are true regarding the medical management of primary hypercalcaemia?
option_A: Use of diuretics could reduce serum calcium levels by increasing their excretion via the kidneys.
option_B: Cinacalcet is a bisphosphonate used to reduce calcium levels.
option_C: Palmidronate is a bisphosphonate used to reduce calcium levels.
option_D: Intravenous saline is the first line of management in hypercalcaemia.
option_E: Serum calcium over 3.5 mmol/L is a medical emergency.
answer_text: Palmidronate is a bisphosphonate used to reduce calcium levels. | Intravenous saline is the first line of management in hypercalcaemia. | Serum calcium over 3.5 mmol/L is a medical emergency.
explanation: Palmidronate, IV saline and calcium >3.5 mmol/L being an emergency are true; diuretics and cinacalcet are not used as stated.

stem: A 54-year-old female presents with a right preauricular lump slowly growing over 5 years. Workup is shown below. What are these studies?
explanation: The studies are T1 and T2 MRI sequences.

stem: What are the findings?
option_A: A cystic lesion in the parotid gland
option_B: Enlargement of the right parotid gland
option_C: A mass in the submandibular gland
answer_text: Enlargement of the right parotid gland
explanation: Imaging shows enlargement of the parotid gland.

stem: What is the next step to reach the diagnosis?
option_B: Fine needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) of the parotid gland
answer_text: Fine needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) of the parotid gland
explanation: FNAB is the appropriate next step for tissue diagnosis.

stem: The previous test results were inconclusive, and her surgeon advised her for surgery. What is the best surgical option?
explanation: Superficial parotidectomy is preferred when tests are inconclusive.

stem: Postoperatively the patient has difficulty in closing her right eye. Explain.
option_A: This is due to damage to the optic nerve
option_B: This is due to injury to the facial nerve during parotidectomy
option_C: This is a complication of general anesthesia
option_D: This is due to local infection
option_E: This is due to a stroke
answer_text: This is due to injury to the facial nerve during parotidectomy
explanation: Facial nerve injury is a known risk during parotid surgery.

stem: If the final histopathology was malignant, what is the next step in managing this lady?
option_C: Radical parotidectomy since it is indicated in patients with clear histological evidence of malignancy
answer_text: Radical parotidectomy since it is indicated in patients with clear histological evidence of malignancy
explanation: Radical parotidectomy is indicated for malignant lesions.

stem: Eight years later, the patient presents with a right submandibular mass. What is this lump and what is the cause?
option_C: Enlargement of the submandibular gland due to the development of a new tumor or spread of cancer cells from the previous parotid gland malignancy
answer_text: Enlargement of the submandibular gland due to the development of a new tumor or spread of cancer cells from the previous parotid gland malignancy
explanation: The mass suggests a new tumor or metastasis from prior malignancy.

stem: How can you prove the diagnosis?
explanation: FNAB is the investigation of choice to confirm the diagnosis.

stem: What is the treatment now?
option_C: Surgical excision & chemotherapy to prevent recurrence
answer_text: Surgical excision & chemotherapy to prevent recurrence
explanation: Recurrent malignant salivary tumour: surgical excision with neck dissection, then adjuvant (chemo)radiotherapy; chemotherapy alone has a limited role.

stem: A 31-year-old male is complaining of a painful swelling on the right side of his neck below the jaw that started a few days ago. He has experienced similar episodes in the past, which resolved spontaneously but were short in duration. The pain worsens when eating sour food. What is the imaging study and what are the findings?
option_A: CT scan showing a lymph node enlargement
option_C: Submandibular sialography reveals a filling defect in the submandibular gland, indicating a potential obstruction or stone in the duct
option_D: MRI of the neck showing a tumor
answer_text: Submandibular sialography reveals a filling defect in the submandibular gland, indicating a potential obstruction or stone in the duct
explanation: Sialography demonstrates a filling defect consistent with a sialolith.

stem: What is the treatment?
option_C: Conservative treatment if the sialolith is small, including removal through the duct orifice with bimanual palpation, heat application, and antibiotics; or sialendoscopy/surgical excision if necessary
answer_text: Conservative treatment if the sialolith is small, including removal through the duct orifice with bimanual palpation, heat application, and antibiotics; or sialendoscopy/surgical excision if necessary
explanation: Treatment is based on stone size; small stones can be managed conservatively.

stem: After a while, the patient came with a weird smile on one side of his face, what is the diagnosis?
option_C: Injury to the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve during submandibular gland excision
answer_text: Injury to the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve during submandibular gland excision
explanation: An asymmetric smile after submandibular gland surgery is weakness of depressor anguli oris from injury to the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve.

stem: A 76-year-old man presents with a rapidly growing lump in his neck causing difficulty swallowing. Examination reveals a 4 cm hard mass in the front of the neck fixed to the overlying skin. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A rapidly enlarging, fixed thyroid mass in an elderly patient suggests anaplastic carcinoma.

stem: A 12-year-old girl notices a painless swelling on the left side of her neck after a recent cold. On examination, it is smooth, fluctuant, non-tender, anterior to the sternocleidomastoid. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A painless, fluctuant swelling in the anterior triangle consistent with a branchial cyst.

stem: A 41-year-old woman presents with a 1-week history of tiredness, muscle aches, neck pain, and restlessness. On examination, she has a smooth enlarged thyroid and a heart rate of 120/min. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A painful subacute thyroiditis with transient hyperthyroid features, often viral in origin.

stem: A 17-year-old boy has paroxysmal sweating, anxiety, palpitations, and a history of a thyroid tumour. He is tall and thin with long fingers. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: MEN IIb: medullary thyroid carcinoma, phaeochromocytoma, marfanoid habitus, mucosal neuromas.
topics: MEN syndromes; Medullary thyroid carcinoma; Phaeochromocytoma

stem: A 12-month-old girl has a large mass in the right side of her neck noticed for months. It is fleshy, compressible, and lies posterior to the sternocleidomastoid. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A congenital lymphatic lesion in the posterior triangle of the neck, often transilluminates.

stem: A 21-year-old man collapses after dizziness and right arm pain while sanding a table. A bony lump is palpable in the right side of his neck. Neurological and vascular exams are normal now. Most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Cervical rib compresses subclavian artery causing vertebral artery flow reversal under exertion.

stem: A 72-year-old man presents with difficulty swallowing and regurgitation of food. He has also had several chest infections over the last few months. On examination, you see a soft swelling in the anterior triangle of the neck. On palpation, the swelling makes a gurgling sound. What is the most likely cause of his dysphagia?
explanation: A pharyngeal (Zenker) pouch can cause dysphagia, regurgitation, halitosis, and a gurgling neck swelling.

stem: A 42-year-old man presents to the GP with a slowly enlarging mass in the left side of his neck which has been present for 3 months. On examination, the mass is 2 cm in diameter, non-tender, pulsatile and can be moved from side to side, but not up or down. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Carotid body tumors (chemodectomas) are pulsatile, move side to side, and lie at the bifurcation.

stem: A 36-year-old woman presents to the GP with a 2-month history of tremors. This is interfering with her work as a typist and the worry has caused her to lose over a stone in weight over the last few weeks. On examination, the thyroid appears normal although a bruit can be heard overlying it. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: An autoimmune hyperthyroidism with a diffuse goitre and bruit is classic for Graves disease.

stem: A 58-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department having been found unresponsive by her husband at home. On examination, you note that she is overweight with coarse features. Observations include heart rate 42/min, blood pressure 100/68 mmHg and temperature 34.6°C. Which of the following would be the most appropriate next step in your management?
explanation: Myxoedema coma requires urgent IV thyroxine and supportive care.

stem: A 32-year-old man presents to the GP with multiple lesions on his trunk which have appeared over the last few months. Each lesion is raised, firm and rubbery, and causes a tingling sensation when touched. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Benign nerve sheath tumours that can present as firm, rubbery skin lesions.

stem: A 42-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with swelling and redness in her left cheek and malaise which has been present for 1 day. On examination, the area of erythema is well demarcated and is hot to touch. Her observations include: heart rate 106/min, blood pressure 108/68 mmHg and temperature 38.6°C. Which of the following is the best course of management?
explanation: Erysipelas is a superficial streptococcal infection often managed with IV antibiotics if severe.

stem: A 46-year-old woman attends her general practice complaining of low mood and tiredness. She has had this for a few months and has had to take time off work. On further questioning she admits to being constipated and to having gained 2 stone in weight over the previous month. On examination, no abnormality is apparent in the neck and no lymphadenopathy is palpable. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Spontaneous atrophic hypothyroidism with typical features of weight gain, constipation, low mood.

stem: You are called to see a 52-year-old woman who has just undergone a thyroidectomy. She complains of a 20-minute history of neck pain and shortness of breath. A rapidly expanding mass is noted around the operation site. Which of the following would you do next?
explanation: Expanding haematoma threatening the airway requires immediate release of sutures.

stem: A 6-year-old girl is brought to the GP by her father with a smooth lump in the midline of her neck. She is otherwise well. On examination, there is a 1 cm painless, fluctuant swelling which moves upwards on swallowing and on tongue protrusion. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Midline cystic swelling moves on tongue protrusion, consistent with thyroglossal duct remnant.

stem: A 19-year-old man presents with a penetrating wound to the right neck (zone II), with hematoma, odynophagia, and violation of the platysma. Vascular and aerodigestive injury is suspected. Which of the following is the best next step?
option_A: intubation and observation in the ICU
option_B: admission to the ICU for close observation without intubation
option_C: observation in the ICU only if carotid angiogram is normal
option_D: observation in the ICU only if carotid angiogram, contrast esophagram, and bronchoscopy are normal
explanation: Zone II penetrating neck trauma with clinical signs mandates surgical exploration.

stem: A 39-year-old woman presents with a palpable 2.5-cm nodule in the left thyroid lobe. She has a history of low-dose chest irradiation in infancy. Which part of her history increases the risk for thyroid cancer?
explanation: Past low-dose irradiation is a known risk factor for thyroid cancer.

stem: For the same thyroid nodule, what is the most appropriate next step in management?
option_D: CT scan of the neck and chest
explanation: FNA is the most accurate diagnostic test for thyroid nodules.

stem: A previously healthy 45-year-old man presents with a 9-month history of a slow-growing, painless right neck mass over the angle of the mandible. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A discrete, slow-growing neck mass in this location is most consistent with a pleomorphic adenoma.

stem: What is the best next step in management for the neck mass described above?
explanation: Definitive treatment of pleomorphic adenoma is superficial parotidectomy.

stem: A 52-year-old woman presents with a calcium level of 11.5 mg/dL found on routine labs. What is the most appropriate next step?
option_A: Repeat her calcium level next year at her annual physical.
option_B: Reassure patient that a calcium level of 11.5 mg/dL is normal.
option_C: Repeat her calcium level and obtain a parathyroid hormone (PTH) level.
option_D: Obtain a CT scan of her neck.
option_E: Obtain positron emission tomography (PET) scan to look for bony metastases.
answer_text: Repeat her calcium level and obtain a parathyroid hormone (PTH) level.
explanation: Workup for hyperparathyroidism includes repeat calcium and PTH assay.

stem: A 22-year-old man has a 2-cm thyroid nodule. His father, now deceased, had thyroid carcinoma and an abdominal tumour. Calcitonin is raised and fine-needle aspiration shows spindle cells with amyloid stroma. Which type of thyroid carcinoma is this?
explanation: Raised calcitonin with amyloid stroma is medullary carcinoma (parafollicular C cells); a familial pattern suggests MEN2 (RET).

stem: A 22-year-old man has a 2-cm thyroid nodule. His family history includes thyroid carcinoma and an unknown abdominal tumour in his father, now deceased; his BP is 145/90 mmHg. Fine-needle aspiration shows medullary thyroid carcinoma. Screening for which of the following must be undertaken before treatment of the thyroid carcinoma?
explanation: Familial medullary carcinoma suggests MEN2: exclude phaeochromocytoma (plasma metanephrines) first, as an unrecognised tumour can cause a fatal crisis at thyroidectomy.
topics: Phaeochromocytoma; Medullary thyroid carcinoma; MEN syndromes

stem: Which of the following is the minimal treatment for the patient’s thyroid carcinoma?
explanation: Total thyroidectomy is the treatment for medullary carcinoma.

stem: Screening for abnormalities in which protooncogene should be offered to his siblings?
explanation: RET gene mutations are associated with MEN II.

stem: A 65-year-old woman evaluated for depression with a history of a recent kidney stone has hypercalcemia and elevated PTH. What is the most likely etiology?
option_C: multiple endocrine neoplasia type I (MEN I)
option_D: multiple endocrine neoplasia type IIa (MEN IIa)
explanation: A parathyroid adenoma is the common cause in older women.

source: Ministerial Evaluation Exam - Head and Neck
stem: A 20-year-old male presented with a tender and fixed swelling in the submandibular region associated with fever and malaise. Three days prior, a dental abscess was drained due to dental caries. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: History of dental abscess drainage with consequent reactive lymphadenopathy.

stem: A 33-year-old pregnant woman presents with weight loss, palpitations, and increased anxiety over the past 3 months. Physical examination reveals a diffusely enlarged vascular thyroid gland, and mild exophthalmos. Thyroid function tests indicate elevated free T3 and T4 levels, with suppressed TSH. Thyroid scan: diffuse increased uptake of both lobes. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
option_A: Immediate surgical intervention with total thyroidectomy.
explanation: Propylthiouracil is preferred in pregnancy for hyperthyroidism.

stem: A 35-year-old female presented with loss of weight and palpitation. Examination revealed fine tremor in the hands and bulging eyes. Which of the following antibodies is diagnostic of this condition?
explanation: TSH receptor antibodies confirm Graves’ disease.

stem: A 46-year-old professional singer had a left thyroid lobectomy for a large thyroid nodule with compression symptoms. Postoperatively, she notices that she is having trouble hitting some notes and projecting her voice. The ligation of which vessel most likely had resulted in this nerve injury?
explanation: Ligation of the superior thyroid artery may injure the external laryngeal nerve, affecting voice.

stem: A 45-year-old woman complains to her primary care physician of nervousness, sweating, tremulousness, and weight loss. The thyroid scan shown here exhibits a pattern that is most consistent with which of the following disorders?
explanation: The thyroid scan shows a single focus of increased isotope uptake, consistent with hypersecreting thyroid nodule.

stem: A 35-year-old woman with a history of previous right thyroidectomy for a benign thyroid nodule now undergoes completion thyroidectomy for a suspicious thyroid mass. Several hours postoperatively, she develops progressive swelling under the incision, stridor, and difficulty breathing. Orotracheal intubation is successful. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
option_A: Fiberoptic laryngoscopy to rule out bilateral vocal cord paralysis
option_C: Administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics and debridement of the wound
option_E: Administration of high-dose steroids and antihistamines
explanation: The clinical presentation is consistent with a wound hematoma and necessitates exploration of the wound, drainage.

stem: A 52-year-old woman sees her physician with complaints of fatigue, headache, flank pain, hematuria, and abdominal pain. She undergoes a sestamibi scan that demonstrates persistent uptake in the right superior parathyroid gland at 2 hours. Which of the following laboratory values is most suggestive of her diagnosis?
explanation: Elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels in conjunction with elevated calcium levels are diagnostic for hyperparathyroidism.

stem: A55-year-old woman presents with a slow-growing painless mass in her neck. A complete neck ultrasound demonstrates a 1-cm nodule in the right thyroid without masses in the contralateral lobe or lymph node metastasis in the central and lateral neck compartments. A fine-needle aspiration of the nodule shows a well-differentiated papillary carcinoma. With regards to this patient, which of the following is associated with a poor prognosis?
explanation: In differentiated thyroid cancer, age is the strongest prognostic factor (AJCC 8th: ≥55 years is high risk); a 1-cm node-negative tumour otherwise has an excellent outlook.

stem: A55-year-old woman presents with a 6-cm right thyroid mass and palpable cervical lymphadenopathy. Fine-needle aspiration (FNA) of one of the lymph nodes demonstrates the presence of thyroid tissue. Which of the following best describes the management of this thyroid disorder?
option_A: Screening for pancreatic endocrine neoplasms and hypercalcemia
option_B: Total thyroidectomy with modified radical neck dissection
option_C: Total thyroidectomy with frozen section intraoperatively, with modified radical neck dissection reserved for patients with extra-capsular invasion
option_D: Right thyroid lobectomy followed by iodine 131 (131I) therapy
answer_text: Total thyroidectomy with modified radical neck dissection
explanation: Treatment of high-risk papillary carcinomas consists of total thyroidectomy with modified radical neck dissection.

stem: A53-year-old woman presents with complaints of weakness, anorexia, malaise, constipation, and back pain. While being evaluated, she becomes somewhat lethargic. Laboratory studies include a normal chest x-ray, serum albumin 3.2 mg/dL, serum calcium 14 mg/dL, serum phosphorus 2.6 mg/dL, serum chloride 108 mg/dL, blood urea nitrogen (BUN) 32 mg/dL, and creatinine 2.0 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
explanation: The initial management of hypercalcemia involves intravenous normal saline to restore intravascular volume and promote renal calcium excretion.

stem: Which of the following patients with primary hyperparathyroidism should undergo parathyroidectomy?
option_B: A54-year-old woman with fatigue and depression
option_C: A42-year-old woman with a history of kidney stones
option_D: A59-year-old woman with mildly elevated 24-hour urinary calcium excretion
option_E: A60-year-old woman with mildly decreased bone mineral density measured at the hip of less than 2 standard deviations below peak bone density
answer_text: A42-year-old woman with a history of kidney stones
explanation: Patients with symptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism, such as those with kidney stones, should undergo parathyroidectomy.

stem: A29-year-old woman with a history of difficulty becoming pregnant presents to her primary care physician and is diagnosed with Graves disease on iodine uptake scan; her thyrotropin (TSH) level is markedly suppressed and her free thyroxine (T4) level is elevated. She desires to conceive as soon as possible and elects to undergo thyroidectomy. After she is rendered euthyroid with medications preoperatively, which of the following management strategies should also be employed to reduce the risk of developing thyroid storm in the operating room?
option_A: Drops of Lugol iodine solution daily beginning 10 days preoperatively
option_B: Preoperative treatment with phenoxybenzamine for 3 weeks
option_C: Preoperative treatment with propranolol for 1 week
option_E: No other preoperative medication is required
answer_text: Drops of Lugol iodine solution daily beginning 10 days preoperatively
explanation: Drops of Lugol iodine solution daily beginning 10 days preoperatively reduce thyroid hormone synthesis and vascularity, lowering the risk of thyroid storm.

stem: A30-year-old woman presents with hypertension, weakness, bone pain, and a serum calcium level of 15.2 mg/dL. Plain films of bilateral hands show osteitis fibrosa cystica. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?
explanation: Osteitis fibrosa cystica is a condition associated with primary hyperparathyroidism, characterized by hypercalcemia and high PTH levels.

stem: A35-year-old woman presents with a serum calcium level of 15.2 mg/ dL and an elevated parathyroid hormone level. Following correction of the patient’s hypercalcemia with hydration and furosemide, which of the following is the best therapeutic approach?
option_C: Neck exploration and resection of all 4 parathyroid glands
option_D: Neck exploration and resection of a parathyroid adenoma
option_E: Avoidance of sunlight, vitamin D, and calcium-containing dairy products
answer_text: Neck exploration and resection of a parathyroid adenoma
explanation: Primary hyperparathyroidism is typically treated surgically with neck exploration and resection of the affected parathyroid gland (adenoma).

stem: A58-year-old man presents with tachycardia, fever, confusion, and vomiting. Workup reveals markedly elevated (triiodothyronine) T3 and (thyroxine) T4 levels. He is diagnosed as having a thyroid storm. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management of this patient?
option_D: Administration of fluid, antithyroid drugs, β-blockers, iodine solution, and steroids
option_E: Emergent radiation therapy to the neck
answer_text: Administration of fluid, antithyroid drugs, β-blockers, iodine solution, and steroids
explanation: Thyroid storm requires immediate management with fluid replacement, antithyroid drugs, β-blockers, iodine solutions, and steroids.

stem: A36-year-old woman, 20 weeks pregnant, presents with a 1.5-cm right thyroid mass. FNA is consistent with a papillary neoplasm. The mass is cold on scan and solid on ultrasound. Which of the following methods of treatment is contraindicated in this patient?
option_D: Total thyroidectomy with lymph node dissection
option_E: 131I radioactive ablation of the thyroid gland
answer_text: 131I radioactive ablation of the thyroid gland
explanation: Radioactive iodine (131I) is contraindicated in pregnancy as it can cross the placenta and harm the fetal thyroid.

stem: A63-year-old woman notices lumps on both sides of her neck. A fine-needle aspirate is nondiagnostic, and she undergoes total thyroidectomy. Final pathology reveals a 4-cm Hürthle cell carcinoma. Which of the following is the most appropriate postsurgical management of this patient?
option_E: Chemotherapy, external beam radiotherapy, and radioiodine ablation
explanation: The treatment of Hürthle cell carcinoma involves surgical resection followed by radioiodine ablation to reduce recurrence risk.

stem: A51-year-old man presents with a 2-cm left thyroid nodule. Thyroid scan shows a cold lesion. FNA cytology demonstrates follicular cells. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment of this patient?
option_A: External beam radiation to the neck
option_D: Prophylactic neck dissection is indicated along with a total thyroidectomy
explanation: For follicular neoplasms, thyroid lobectomy is the initial treatment to assess capsular or vascular invasion on histology, which determines malignancy.

stem: A 52-year-old woman presents with a history of abdominal pain and constipation. As part of her workup, she was noted to have a calcium level of 12 mg/dL. For each of the following test results, choose the most appropriate etiology of hypercalcemia. Each lettered option may be used once, more than once, or not at all. Genetic testing showing mutation in a tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 11q12-13
explanation: Mutation in tumor suppressor gene on 11q12-13 is associated with parathyroid hyperplasia.

stem: Low 24-hour urinary calcium level (<100 mg/d)
explanation: Low 24-hour urinary calcium is indicative of familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia (FHH).

stem: Serum calcium level 15 mg/dL and parathyroid hormone level 5 times normal
explanation: High calcium and markedly elevated PTH suggest parathyroid carcinoma.

stem: Very low level of intact PTH
explanation: Low PTH in hypercalcemia suggests a paraneoplastic syndrome, likely PTHrP production.

stem: What is the necessary drop in intraoperative PTH during parathyroidectomy?
explanation: A fall in PTH of at least 50% from the highest pre-excision value 10 minutes after gland removal (Miami criterion) predicts cure.

stem: An 18-year-old school student of East African origin presents with a 2-week history of lethargy, myalgia, rigours with hot flushes and intermittent pyrexia. Neither she nor any close contacts have been travelling recently. Examination reveals enlarged anterior and posterior chain lymph nodes in the neck. A blood film reveals the presence of Downey bodies, thrombocytosis and an increase in the lymphocyte count to 50% of total leucocytes. This girl is likely to have
explanation: Infectious mononucleosis is caused by Epstein–Barr virus, resulting in reactive lymphocytosis with Downey bodies; diagnosis is usually confirmed by a positive Monospot test.

stem: A 16-year-old girl presents with a smooth, round and painless lump in the midline of the neck, of which she feels very self‐conscious. On examination, it is firm, transilluminates and is painless to touch. In addition, it moves up when the patient is asked to take a sip of water. This is likely to be a
explanation: Thyroglossal cysts are remnants of the thyroglossal duct that move with swallowing and are managed by surgical excision.

stem: A 45-year-old female business executive presents with a swelling in the midline of the neck and features of hyperthyroidism secondary to Graves’ disease. Following a course of antithyroid medication, a subtotal thyroidectomy is performed. Raised titres of which immunoglobulin would be expected in this individual?
explanation: Graves’ disease is associated with increased anti-TSH receptor antibodies.

stem: You are asked to assess a 25-year-old patient who returned from theatre 2 hours ago following a thyroidectomy for a large, hyperplastic goitre and is now complaining of difficulty swallowing sips of water. On examination you note that she is very short of breath with a respiratory rate of 30 breaths/min, using her accessory muscles of respiration and only able to answer your questions in two or three words. In addition, there appears to be a fluctuant mass in the midline of the neck underlying the surgical clips. Immediate management of this patient would be
option_B: Removal of surgical clips at the bedside
option_C: Intravenous access with two large-bore cannulae and fluid resuscitation
option_D: Removal of surgical clips in theatre under general anaesthesia
option_E: Call your senior and wait for him/her to remove the clips
answer_text: Removal of surgical clips at the bedside
explanation: Airway compromise from a tension hematoma post-thyroidectomy necessitates immediate bedside clip removal.

stem: A 28-year-old secretary presents with a lump in the midline of the neck that has grown progressively larger over the past several months. On examination, there is a palpable lymph node in the left submandibular region. An aspirate is taken, confirming a malignant cancer of the thyroid gland. The origin of this is most likely to be
explanation: Papillary carcinoma is the most common thyroid cancer, often multifocal and typically spreads via lymphatics.

stem: A 37-year-old patient is diagnosed with medullary carcinoma of the thyroid gland. The concentration of which electrolyte could be reduced in this patient?
explanation: Medullary carcinoma produces calcitonin from C cells, which lowers serum calcium levels.

stem: A 68-year-old man presents with a 10-week history of a rapidly growing swelling in the midline of the neck. Prior to this problem developing he has been in excellent health. Over the past 10 weeks, he has begun to feel more worn out and is unable to complete his daily 3-mile walk without getting short of breath, which he was previously able to manage comfortably. His wife also reports that his voice has become increasingly hoarse in the last 2 weeks. The presentation is likely to be consistent with
explanation: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is aggressive, with rapid growth and compressive symptoms such as hoarseness and breathlessness.

stem: A 59-year-old fisherman presents with longstanding weight loss, anorexia and lethargy. Physical examination reveals a palpable swelling in the left supraclavicular fossa. A disseminated adenocarcinoma of the stomach is diagnosed following a gastroscopy and computed tomography scan of the thorax and abdomen. This patient has presented with
explanation: An enlarged left supraclavicular node (Troisier’s sign) suggests metastatic spread from an abdominal malignancy such as gastric adenocarcinoma.

stem: Which of the following structures does not form a border of the anterior triangle of the neck?
explanation: The middle third of the clavicle is not included as a border of the anterior triangle of the neck.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: A 60-year-old retired nurse presents with weight loss, fainting episodes, and tiredness. A blood glucose is 2.5 mmol/L and an insulinoma is suspected. Which of the following tests are appropriate?
answer_text: Insulin levels. | C-peptide levels. | A 24-hour fast.
explanation: High insulin and C-peptide during a 24-hour fast confirm an insulinoma; synacthen test is not indicated.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following statements are true? (MEN Epidemiology and Genetics)
option_A: MEN1 is characterised by tumours in the pituitary, pancreas and parathyroids.
option_B: Medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) plays a key role in MEN2 subtypes.
option_C: The mode of inheritance is autosomal dominant in both MEN1 and 2.
option_D: The penetrance of the mutation is low.
option_E: Screening of family members of the affected individual is essential.
answer_text: MEN1 is characterised by tumours in the pituitary, pancreas and parathyroids. | Medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) plays a key role in MEN2 subtypes. | The mode of inheritance is autosomal dominant in both MEN1 and 2. | Screening of family members of the affected individual is essential.
explanation: MEN1 and MEN2 are autosomal dominant with high penetrance; screening is essential and tumours involve the pituitary, pancreas, parathyroids and MTC in MEN2.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: The following statements are true except: (MEN1 Clinical Presentation)
option_A: Nephrolithiasis is a common clinical presentation.
option_B: Pancreatic endocrine tumours (PET) are a common cause of death.
option_C: Insulinomas are the most common pancreatic tumours in MEN1.
option_D: All pituitary tumours must be surgically resected.
answer_text: Insulinomas are the most common pancreatic tumours in MEN1. | All pituitary tumours must be surgically resected. | Adrenocortical carcinomas frequently develop.
explanation: False: Insulinomas are not most common, not all pituitary tumours require surgery and adrenocortical carcinoma is rare in MEN1.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following statements are true? (Surgical Treatment in MEN1)
option_A: Selective resection of the parathyroid is a preferred treatment option.
option_B: MEN1 gastrinomas and insulinomas must be operated on.
option_C: All nonfunctional adrenal tumours can be left alone.
option_D: All nonfunctional PETs can be left alone.
option_E: Most procedures related to the pituitary can be performed through the trans-sphenoidal approach.
answer_text: MEN1 gastrinomas and insulinomas must be operated on. | Most procedures related to the pituitary can be performed through the trans-sphenoidal approach.
explanation: Functional pancreatic tumours require surgery and pituitary procedures are mainly trans-sphenoidal.

source: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following statements are true? (MEN2)
option_A: MTC is a late manifestation of MEN2a.
option_B: Primary hyperparathyroidism (pHPT) is an early manifestation of MEN2.
option_C: Diagnostic work-up for MEN2 must include scintigraphy.
option_D: Mutation carriers of MEN2 must be offered a thyroidectomy.
option_E: Unilateral or bilateral sub-total resection of a phaeochromocytoma in MEN2 is appropriate.
answer_text: Diagnostic work-up for MEN2 must include scintigraphy. | Mutation carriers of MEN2 must be offered a thyroidectomy. | Unilateral or bilateral sub-total resection of a phaeochromocytoma in MEN2 is appropriate.
explanation: In MEN2, scintigraphy is used, prophylactic thyroidectomy is advised and subtotal resection of phaeochromocytoma is acceptable; the other statements are false.

stem: A 35-year-old woman has been recently diagnosed by her GP with . Graves’ disease and has been referred to the outpatient department for further management. She has no other past medical history. She is a housewife and looks after her three young children aged 1 to 6. She has a large goitre with signs of severe exophthalmos (see Figure 5.1). Which is the single most appropriate long term treatment option for this lady?
explanation: Graves disease with severe ophthalmopathy is best treated surgically (now usually total thyroidectomy); radioiodine can worsen the eye disease and drugs alone often relapse.

stem: A 50-year-old woman has had 3 weeks of pain in front of her neck. She also complains of general malaise, episodes of feeling feverish, and palpitations. She has no past medical history and is not on any regular medications. She has a diffusely tender, slightly enlarged thyroid gland. Which is the single most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Painful tender swelling of the thyroid is suggestive of de Quervain’s thyroiditis.

stem: A 90-year-old woman has a swelling in her neck which has increased in size over the last 2 weeks. She reports difficulty in swallowing, shortness of breath, coughing, and a hoarse voice. She has a large fixed mass in the left anterior triangle of her neck with palpable cervical lymphadenopathy. Which is the single most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Anaplastic carcinoma is most likely due to large fixed mass and lymphadenopathy.

stem: A 35-year-old woman has had a painful lump in her neck for 1 month. She has no other related symptoms. She has a solitary thyroid nodule that is slightly tender. A fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) gives a result of Thy2. Which is the single most likely diagnosis?
explanation: FNAB result Thy2 indicates a benign colloid nodule.

stem: A 40-year-old woman has undergone a total thyroidectomy for a multinodular goitre. She is a member of her local choir and has noticed that she is no longer able to reach high notes as she used to prior to her surgery and that her voice fatigues. Which is the single most likely nerve that has been injured at surgery?
explanation: Injury to the external laryngeal nerve impairs high-pitched voice production.

stem: Figure 5.2 is a graphic illustration of the formation of various thyroid hormones by thyroid epithelial cells. I- is ionic iodine, deI indicates the process of de-iodinization, and AA circulating amino acids. Four structurally different hormones are indicated by the letters W, X, Y, and Z. Which is the single correct name of the hormone X?
explanation: Hormone X corresponds to Tri-iodothyronine (T3).

stem: A 40-year-old man has had 1 month of spontaneous episodes of palpitations, headaches, sweating, and chest pain lasting for up to 15min. A diagnosis of phaeochromocytoma is considered. Which is the single most appropriate initial investigation that will help to confirm the diagnosis?
explanation: Catecholamine excess is confirmed biochemically first (plasma free or 24-h urinary metanephrines; here 24-h urinary VMA/noradrenaline), then the tumour is localised by CT/MRI.

stem: A 65-year-old woman is referred by her GP following a routine blood test which showed a raised serum calcium. Over the last few months she has become constipated with intermittent bouts of abdominal pain. She is lethargic and her mood has been very low. Clinical examination is unremarkable. Biochemical results show a corrected serum calcium of 2.95mmol/L and a serum parathyroid hormone of 24pmol/L. Which is the single most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Primary hyperparathyroidism is indicated by raised calcium and PTH levels.

stem: A 65-year-old man has recently gained a significant amount of weight, his hair has become very dry and brittle, and his mood is low. He has a round face with a prominent fat pad along his back. Which is the single most appropriate subsequent investigation?
explanation: Clinical signs indicate Cushing’s syndrome; dexamethasone suppression test is appropriate.

stem: A 15-year-old otherwise healthy female high school student begins to notice galactorrhea. A pregnancy test is negative. Which of the following is a frequently associated physical finding?
explanation: Prolactin-secreting tumors in the pituitary gland may cause bitemporal hemianopia because of compression of the optic chiasm.

stem: A 53-year-old woman presents with weight loss and a persistent rash to her lower abdomen and perineum. She is diagnosed with necrolytic migrating erythema and additional workup demonstrates a hemoglobin A1c of 7.5%, hematocrit of 26%, and a large mass in the tail of the pancreas. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A large pancreatic tail mass with necrolytic migrating erythema is consistent with glucagonoma.

stem: A50-year-old man presents with intractable peptic ulcer disease, severe esophagitis, and abdominal pain. Which of the following is most consistent with the diagnosis of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome?
option_D: Increase in gastrin level (>200 pg/mL) after administration of secretin
option_E: Decrease in gastrin level (>200 pg/mL) after administration of secretin
answer_text: Increase in gastrin level (>200 pg/mL) after administration of secretin
explanation: A paradoxical increase in serum gastrin after administration of secretin is diagnostic of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.

stem: A34-year-old woman has recurrent fainting spells induced by fasting. She also reports palpitations, trembling, diaphoresis, and confusion prior to the syncopal episodes. She has relief of symptoms with the administration of glucose. Which of the following findings is most consistent with the diagnosis of an insulinoma?
option_A: Serum glucose level >50 mg/dL, elevated serum insulin levels, elevated C-peptide levels
option_B: Serum glucose level >50 mg/dL, elevated serum insulin levels, decreased C-peptide levels
option_C: Serum glucose level <50 mg/dL, elevated serum insulin levels, elevated C-peptide levels
option_D: Serum glucose level <50 mg/dL, elevated serum insulin levels, decreased C-peptide levels
option_E: Serum glucose level <50 mg/dL, decreased serum insulin levels, decreased C-peptide levels
answer_text: Serum glucose level <50 mg/dL, elevated serum insulin levels, elevated C-peptide levels
explanation: In insulinoma, endogenous insulin production leads to low glucose, high insulin, and high C-peptide levels.

stem: A 28-year-old woman, who was hospitalized 2 months ago following a head injury, attends the outpatient clinic with a 6-week history of polyuria and polydipsia and no other symptoms. Her blood pressure is 117/83 mmHg and her heart rate is 68 beats/min. From the list below, select the most appropriate management option.
explanation: Central diabetes insipidus post-head injury is treated with desmopressin.

stem: During a ward round, you are asked by your surgical registrar about the management of a phaeochromocytoma. Select from the list below the most appropriate management plan for a phaeochromocytoma.
option_A: Surgical resection, followed by β blockade, followed by α blockade
option_D: β blockade, followed by α blockade, followed by surgical resection
option_E: α blockade, followed by β blockade followed by surgical resection
answer_text: α blockade, followed by β blockade followed by surgical resection
explanation: Phaeochromocytoma management requires α blockade, then β blockade, before surgical resection.

explanation: Hypothyroid symptoms of lethargy, constipation, and weight gain indicate primary myxoedema.

explanation: Sudden pain in a pre-existing thyroid nodule suggests haemorrhage into a cyst.

explanation: Tender enlarged thyroid after viral illness indicates de Quervain thyroiditis.

explanation: Weight loss, tachycardia, tremor, and thyroid bruit are characteristic of Graves disease.

explanation: Severe hypothermia, bradycardia, and altered consciousness in untreated hypothyroidism indicate myxoedema coma.

explanation: Riedel thyroiditis causes a fibrotic goitre with benign histology.

explanation: Lymphoma presents as painless lymphadenopathy with systemic symptoms such as weight loss and night sweats. Common in young adults. Diagnosis confirmed by biopsy and imaging.

explanation: Branchial cysts occur along the anterior border of SCM and are fluctuant.

explanation: Lipomas are soft, mobile, painless fatty tumours; can be multiple.
