A further staging computed tomography scan shows no distant metastases. According to the TNM classification, the tumour stage in this individual is
explanation: Invasion into the detrusor muscle is T2; no involved nodes is N0 and no distant spread on CT is M0.

explanation: A small (T1a, ≤ 4 cm) renal cell carcinoma is treated by nephron-sparing partial nephrectomy.

explanation: A non-functioning, chronically infected kidney is removed by simple nephrectomy.

stem: A 70-year-old man on IV antibiotics for 5 days has fever, rigors and flank pain; HR 120, BP 80/60. CT shows hydroureteronephrosis to the mid-ureter.
explanation: An infected obstructed kidney with septic shock needs urgent decompression; percutaneous nephrostomy is safest in the unstable patient.

stem: A 4-year-old girl has recurrent febrile UTIs despite long-term antibiotics; micturating cystogram shows a dilated, tortuous left ureter.
explanation: High-grade vesicoureteric reflux with breakthrough febrile UTIs is treated by ureteric reimplantation.

stem: A 44-year-old man has painless haematuria; CT shows a tumour of the left renal pelvis without metastasis.
explanation: Upper-tract urothelial carcinoma is treated by nephroureterectomy with a bladder cuff.

stem: A 25-year-old woman has dysuria, frequency and suprapubic pain without fever or flank pain. Urine is cloudy with leucocytes and nitrites.
explanation: Lower urinary symptoms without fever or loin pain are acute (uncomplicated) cystitis.

stem: A 60-year-old man has fever, chills and perineal pain; DRE is difficult because of severe anterior rectal tenderness. Urine grows E. coli.
explanation: Fever, perineal pain and an exquisitely tender prostate is acute bacterial prostatitis (avoid prostatic massage).

stem: A 28-year-old diabetic woman has high fever, flank pain, vomiting and renal angle tenderness. CT shows pockets of gas and fluid in the left kidney.
explanation: Gas within the renal parenchyma in a diabetic is emphysematous pyelonephritis: antibiotics, drainage, sometimes nephrectomy.

stem: A 40-year-old man has come to A&E complaining of a sudden onset of very severe pain in his left loin of 4 hours duration, radiating to the front of the lumbar area and groin and the left testis. He has vomited a couple of times and has urinary frequency. On examination he is writhing in pain and cannot find a comfortable position.
option_G: Transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of renal pelvis
explanation: Sudden severe loin pain radiating to the groin and testis, with vomiting and restlessness, is ureteric colic from a ureteric calculus.
topics: Renal colic; Varicocele; Renal cell carcinoma; PUJ obstruction

stem: A 60-year-old man complains of haematuria associated with pain in his left loin radiating to the lower abdomen for about 2 months. He passes clots that are ‘worm-like’. On examination he has an enlarged left kidney, and scrotal examination reveals a varicocele of which he was unaware.
option_G: Transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of renal pelvis
explanation: Haematuria with worm-like clots, loin pain, a renal mass and a new left varicocele (renal vein invasion) indicate renal cell carcinoma.
topics: Renal colic; Varicocele; Renal cell carcinoma; PUJ obstruction

stem: A 45-year-old female patient complains of nagging pain in her right loin and urinary frequency for several months. On examination she has tenderness in her loin over the kidney. Urine examination shows red blood cells and a growth of Proteus and staphylococci.
option_G: Transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of renal pelvis
explanation: Chronic loin pain with Proteus infection (urease-splitting, alkaline urine) suggests a struvite staghorn calculus.
topics: Renal colic; Varicocele; Renal cell carcinoma; PUJ obstruction

stem: A fit 20-year-old young man had a game of rugby, following which he passed frank blood in his urine in the changing room. He felt some discomfort in his left loin. After returning home, his haematuria became worse and he noticed some fullness in his left loin. He then came to A&E. His blood pressure was 110/60 mmHg, his pulse was 110/minute and he had fullness in his left loin.
option_G: Transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of renal pelvis
explanation: Disproportionate haematuria and loin swelling after minor trauma suggest bleeding from an abnormal kidney, classically congenital hydronephrosis (PUJ obstruction).
topics: Renal colic; Varicocele; Renal cell carcinoma; PUJ obstruction

stem: A 60-year-old female patient was seen as an emergency with high temperature, rigors, and pain in her right loin. She had a blood pressure of 160/70 mmHg, bounding pulse of 90/minute, and extreme tenderness in her right loin.
option_G: Transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of renal pelvis
explanation: High fever, rigors and an exquisitely tender loin indicate an infected obstructed kidney (pyonephrosis) needing urgent drainage.
topics: Renal colic; Varicocele; Renal cell carcinoma; PUJ obstruction

stem: A 62-year-old man complains of left loin ache with intermittent painless haematuria in the form of clots, occasional high temperature and rigors, some dysuria, and frequency for 6 months. An IVU shows an irregular filling defect in the lower one-third of the left ureter. There is nothing to find on clinical examination. His Hb is 10.2 gm/dL.
option_G: Transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of renal pelvis
explanation: Haematuria with an irregular filling defect in the lower ureter is urothelial (transitional cell) carcinoma of the ureter until proven otherwise.
topics: Renal colic; Varicocele; Renal cell carcinoma; PUJ obstruction

stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with recurrent attacks of urinary tract infection. On every occasion this was successfully treated with antibiotics. In view of several such episodes in the past, she underwent an IVU, which showed the renal calyces to be pointing toward the vertebrae.
option_G: Transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of renal pelvis
explanation: Calyces pointing medially towards the spine on IVU are characteristic of a horseshoe kidney, which predisposes to infection and stones.
topics: Renal colic; Varicocele; Renal cell carcinoma; PUJ obstruction

stem: A male child of 3 years has been brought by his mother, who noticed while bathing him that the right side of his abdomen felt larger than the left and was asymmetrical; she thought that there was probably a lump in his abdomen.
option_G: Transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of renal pelvis
explanation: An asymptomatic flank mass noticed by a parent in a 3-year-old is classic for Wilms tumour (nephroblastoma).
topics: Renal colic; Varicocele; Renal cell carcinoma; PUJ obstruction

stem: A 10-year-old boy has been brought in as an emergency by his parents as they noticed that he had bright red haematuria for the past 24 hours or so. About 6 hours prior to that he was climbing a tree and accidentally fell on his left side.
option_G: Transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of renal pelvis
explanation: Frank haematuria after a fall on to the loin indicates blunt renal trauma; children's kidneys are relatively unprotected.
